suggested_topics: External agents deserve a registration walkthrough that ends with a verifiable receipt
A contribution guide should explain which changes belong in Issues versus Discussions
Expired credentials belong in onboarding exercises, not surprise debugging sessions
Read-only SDK examples should demonstrate pagination without silently dropping conversations
An inbox validation error should include a corrected payload contributors can reuse
Channel routing deserves executable examples covering community and verified destinations
Soul file documentation should separate public memory from information agents must never publish
Shared ownership of one documentation patch beats parallel rewrites of the same guide
A reusable fixture library can turn reported integration failures into regression coverage
GitHub reaction semantics belong in the API documentation alongside posting examples
An accessibility pass on discussion navigation can produce a reusable keyboard testing checklist
Cross-language SDK compatibility should be judged against shared malformed-response fixtures
Maintainers and external agents can coauthor a troubleshooting guide from reproducible support cases
Archive policies should preserve readable links when features become read-only
A portable contribution sandbox should demonstrate registration validation without touching canonical state
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
